title: How to add a table in Numbers on Mac: the Table button, styles and resizing
metaTitle: How to Add a Table in Numbers on Mac (Step by Step)
description: Learn how to add a table in Numbers on Mac: click the Table button, pick a style, then resize it, add rows and format it in the Format sidebar.
targetKeyword: how to add a table in numbers on mac
intro: To add a table in Numbers on Mac, click the Table button in the toolbar, then pick a style or drag one onto your sheet. Apple's guide calls this a style picker, and it lists no Insert menu entry or keyboard shortcut for adding a table.
tldr: Click the Table button in the Numbers toolbar, then choose a style or drag one onto the sheet.
Move a table with the Table handle in its top-left corner. Add rows with the Add Row button at the bottom-left.
Delete a table by clicking its Table handle and pressing Delete. Rows that hold data need Option-drag.
The steps follow Apple's guide for Numbers 15.4, which needs macOS 26. Check Numbers > About Numbers.

blocks.text: Numbers keeps tables in a different place from most Mac apps. You won't find a table command in an Insert menu, because Apple's Mac guide doesn't list one. The Table button in the toolbar does the job. Click it, pick a style, and the table lands on your sheet. The rest of this page covers what comes after: moving, resizing, adding rows, formatting, locking and fixing the common problems.
Check your Numbers version first

The steps on this page follow Apple's Numbers for Mac guide, which covers Numbers 15.4. To check your version, click Numbers in the menu bar, then choose About Numbers. TidBITS reports that Numbers 15.4 requires macOS 26 Tahoe. If your version is older, the buttons may sit in different places, and this page does not cover older releases.
Apple's release notes for 15.1, 15.3 and 15.4 list no table, row, column, menu or toolbar changes. That suggests the steps match across those releases, but this page is written for 15.4.

items: A Mac that runs macOS 26 Tahoe, the minimum for Numbers 15.4
A Numbers spreadsheet open in front of you
The Format sidebar, which you can show with ⌥⌘I
A table that isn't locked, if you plan to change it

blocks.text: Pick a table style and place it on the sheet

After you click the Table button, a set of table styles opens. Apple calls this a style picker, not a dialog. Swipe to see more styles. Apple's guide also points to a stock-information style in the bottom-right corner of the picker.

Click a style to place it on the sheet, or drag it there. Dragging lets you choose the spot on the first try. Clicking is quicker when the position doesn't matter, because you can move the table afterward with the Table handle. Either way, you can change the table once it is on the sheet.
Move and resize the table

Every table has a Table handle in its top-left corner. Drag that handle to move the table anywhere on the sheet. If you don't see the handle, click the table first. Resizing is a separate step. Click the table, click the Table handle, then Shift-drag the white square in the bottom-right corner. Apple's resize page says resizing changes the size of the table, not the number of rows and columns.

blocks.title: Keep the shape
blocks.text: Hold Shift while you drag the white square in the bottom-right corner. Shift keeps the proportions, so the table grows or shrinks evenly.
Add and remove rows and columns

Adding rows is a drag. Find the Add Row button in the bottom-left corner of the table. Drag it to add rows, and drag it back to remove empty ones. Columns use the Add Column button in the top-right corner, which works the same way. When you need rows and columns at once, drag the bottom-right button. That adds or removes both together.

Numbers also gives you a menu for each row and column. Hover over a row number, click the arrow that appears, and choose Add Rows Above or Add Rows Below. Column letters have the same arrow, with Add Columns Before, Add Columns After and Delete Selected Columns. The menu is quicker when you need a new row in the middle of a table.

rows: Adds a row above the selected cells
Adds a row below the selected cells
Adds a column to the right of the selected cells
Adds a column to the left of the selected cells
blocks.caption: Table shortcuts from Apple's Numbers keyboard shortcut page.

blocks.text: Each shortcut acts on the selected cells. Select a cell next to the spot you want to change, then press the key. Apple notes that some shortcuts can be changed in System Settings, so your keys may differ from this list.
Delete a table or only some rows and columns

To delete a whole table, click the table, click the Table handle in the top-left corner, then press Delete. Look at the sheet before you press it. Once the table is gone, you need the Table button and a new style to get one back.

Rows and columns follow a different rule. Numbers deletes a row or column normally only when every cell in it is empty. To remove rows or columns that hold data, hold Option and drag the bottom-right button. Apple's rows page describes this method, so use it when a plain delete doesn't work.

blocks.title: Linked forms
blocks.text: A table linked to a form made in Numbers for iPhone or iPad loses the form when you delete it. Check for a linked form before you remove the table.
Format headers, footers and alternating colors

Formatting lives in the Format sidebar. Click the table, then open the sidebar with ⌥⌘I if it's hidden. Click the Table tab. Apple's guide puts the header, footer, freeze and color controls there, so you rarely need another menu.

Under Headers & Footers, pop-up menus set header rows, header columns and footer rows. A table can have up to five header rows, five header columns and five footer rows. Freeze Header Rows or Columns sits in the same area. Freezing keeps the header visible when you scroll a long table.

Alternating Row Color adds stripes, which helps readers follow a wide row across the page. Select it in the Table tab. A color well next to it lets you pick a different stripe color. Start with a light stripe, because it is easier to read than a dark one.
Lock a finished table

Locking matters when a table is part of a template that other people fill in. Click the table, open the Arrange menu, and choose Lock. A locked table can't be edited, moved or deleted. To change it, click the table, open the Arrange menu again, and choose the command that switches the lock off. Lock a table only after you finish building it. Locking protects headers and formulas before you share the file.
Table keyboard shortcuts on Mac
Apple's shortcut page covers more than the row and column keys. These are the other table keys worth knowing. Apple lists them for tables and the sidebar, so they help once your table exists.

items: ⌫: deletes a selected table, or the contents of a selected cell
⇥: selects the next cell, and adds a column when you are on the last cell of a row
⌥⌘← and ⌥⌘→: select the first or last populated cell in a row

blocks.text: Keep one warning in mind. The Delete key handles a selected table and a selected cell differently. Select the Table handle when you mean the whole table. Otherwise, you only clear the text in one cell.
Mistakes people make with Numbers tables

items: Looking for an Insert menu entry. Apple's Mac guide lists none, so use the toolbar Table button.
Pressing Delete with one cell selected. That clears the cell, not the table.
Dragging the Table handle when you meant to resize. The handle moves the table, so use the white square in the bottom-right corner.
Using a plain delete on a row with data. Hold Option and drag the bottom-right button instead.
Forgetting that a locked table can't change. Open the Arrange menu and switch the lock off first.
Deleting a table linked to a form. The form is cleared too.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes come from one habit. People treat the table as a single object, when it has several handles, and each one does a different job. Learn which handle does which job, and the table gets much easier to control.
Numbers for iCloud compared with the Mac app

Numbers for iCloud has a Table button too. Apple's guide describes the row handle at the bottom-left, the column handle at the top-right and the bottom-right handle for both. In the browser, the Table tab sits at the top of the Format sidebar.

The browser version has real limits. Apple lists 255 columns, 65,535 rows and about 130,000 cells with data per table on iCloud.com. Tables past those limits can be viewed in the browser but not edited. You also can't create range-based pivot tables there, so use the Mac app for those.
Where to go next with your table

Most tables get sorted or filtered next. This site has a guide for each: [sort a table by column in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/sort-a-table-by-column-in-numbers) and [filter table rows in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/filter-table-rows-in-numbers). When the data is final, [export the spreadsheet to Excel](/how-to/export-a-spreadsheet-to-excel-in-numbers) if someone else needs it.
For more on what Lazur does inside Numbers, see the [Numbers page](/apps/numbers). Hold ⌥⌘ and ask where a button is. Lazur circles it on your screen. Lazur doesn't click the button for you.

faq.question: Is there an Insert menu command for tables in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac guide does not list one. Click the Table button in the toolbar instead. A row of table styles opens, and you pick one to place a table on your sheet.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to add a table in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's keyboard shortcut page lists none for adding a table. The shortcuts it does list add rows and columns to a table you already have, such as ⌥↓ for a row below and ⌥→ for a column to the right.

faq.question: How do I delete a table in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Click the table, click the Table handle in its top-left corner, then press Delete. If the table is linked to a form made in Numbers for iPhone or iPad, deleting it clears the form.

faq.question: Why won't Numbers delete a row that has data in it?
faq.answer: A plain delete only removes rows and columns whose cells are all empty. To remove a row with data, hold Option and drag the bottom-right button. Check the sheet afterward before you keep working.

faq.question: Which version of Numbers does this guide cover?
faq.answer: Apple's Mac guide covers Numbers 15.4. TidBITS reports that Numbers 15.4 requires macOS 26 Tahoe. Check your version under Numbers > About Numbers.

faq.question: Can I keep the header row visible when I scroll?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the Format sidebar, click the Table tab, and turn on Freeze Header Rows or Freeze Header Columns in the Headers & Footers area. A table can have up to five header rows.

faq.question: Can I add a table in Numbers for iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Click the Table button in the toolbar and pick a layout. Browser limits apply, including 255 columns and 65,535 rows per table, and you can't create range-based pivot tables there.

faq.question: Does Lazur add the table for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur doesn't click buttons or work inside Numbers for you. Ask where the Table button is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask for a walkthrough and Lazur guides you one click at a time.

faq.question: Is Lazur an add-in for Numbers?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker.

steps.name: Open the spreadsheet
steps.text: Open Numbers, then open the spreadsheet that should hold the table. Click the sheet tab for the sheet you want. The table goes onto the sheet you have selected, so check the tab first. If you start from a blank sheet, add the table before you type any data.

steps.name: Click the Table button in the toolbar
steps.text: Find the Table button in the toolbar and click it. A row of table styles opens. Apple describes this as a style picker, not a dialog, so there is no confirmation step before the table appears.
steps.tip: Apple's Mac guide lists no Insert menu entry for tables, so look in the toolbar instead.

steps.name: Pick a style or drag one onto the sheet
steps.text: Swipe to see more styles. Apple's guide points to a stock-information style in the bottom-right corner of the picker. Click a style to place it, or drag it onto the sheet and let go where you want it.
steps.tip: Dragging gives you the position on the first try. You can still move the table later.

steps.name: Move the table with the Table handle
steps.text: Find the Table handle in the top-left corner of the table. Drag the handle to move the table anywhere on the sheet. If you don't see the handle, click the table first.
steps.tip: Dragging the Table handle moves the table. It does not change the size.

steps.name: Resize the table and keep its shape
steps.text: Click the table, then click the Table handle. Shift-drag the white square in the bottom-right corner to resize the table proportionally. Resizing changes the size, not the number of rows and columns.
steps.tip: Shift keeps the shape. Resizing does not add or remove rows or columns.

steps.name: Add rows and columns
steps.text: Drag the Add Row button in the bottom-left corner to add rows. Drag the Add Column button in the top-right corner to add columns. For a single row, select a cell and press ⌥↓ to add a row below it. Press ⌥→ to add a column to the right.
steps.tip: Hover over a row number or column letter, then click the small arrow that appears for insert options.

steps.name: Turn on alternating row color
steps.text: Click the table. If the Format sidebar is hidden, press ⌥⌘I to show it. Click the Table tab, then select Alternating Row Color. Use the color well next to it to pick a different stripe color.

steps.name: Set header rows and freeze them
steps.text: In the Table tab, open the Headers & Footers pop-up menus. Set header rows, header columns or footer rows, up to five of each. Turn on Freeze Header Rows or Columns in the same area to keep them visible while you scroll.
steps.tip: Set your headers before you fill in the data, so the table is easier to read as you type.

steps.name: Check your version if the steps differ
steps.text: If a step doesn't match your screen, check the version. Click Numbers in the menu bar, then choose About Numbers. Apple's guide covers Numbers 15.4.
steps.tip: TidBITS reports that Numbers 15.4 requires macOS 26 Tahoe.

troubleshooting.problem: The Table button is missing from the toolbar
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm that a Numbers spreadsheet is open. Then check your version under Numbers > About Numbers, because these steps are written for Numbers 15.4.

troubleshooting.problem: Pressing Delete cleared text but kept the table
troubleshooting.fix: A cell was selected, and Delete clears cell contents. Click the Table handle in the top-left corner first, then press Delete.
A plain delete works only when every cell in the row is empty. Hold Option and drag the bottom-right button to remove a row that holds data.

troubleshooting.problem: The table won't move, resize or change
troubleshooting.fix: The table may be locked. Click the table, open the Arrange menu, and switch the lock off, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: I moved the table when I meant to resize it
troubleshooting.fix: Press ⌘Z to undo the move. Then resize with Shift-drag on the white square in the bottom-right corner, not the Table handle.

troubleshooting.problem: The form is empty after I deleted a table
troubleshooting.fix: Deleting a table linked to a form made in Numbers for iPhone or iPad clears the form. Rebuild the table with the Table button, and check the form before you reuse it.
